title: Improved Performances and Motivation in Intelligent Tutoring Systems: Combining Machine Learning and Learner Choice
extended_summary:
This paper examines whether an AI-driven intelligent tutoring system can improve both learning outcomes and motivation in early elementary mathematics, and whether giving children limited choice within the tutoring interface adds further benefits. The authors focus on a known tension in educational technology: personalized adaptive sequencing may improve learning, but it is unclear whether adding gamified choice helps or hurts when combined with different curriculum structures.

The intervention is KidLearn / ZPDES, an intelligent tutoring system that uses a learning-progress-based multi-armed bandit approach to adaptively select exercises within a zone-of-proximal-development framework. The study compares four conditions: a predefined linear sequence with and without learner choice, and the adaptive ZPDES sequence with and without learner choice. Choice is contextual and orthogonal to difficulty, involving selection of visual objects used in the exercises rather than selecting easier or harder tasks. The trial involved 265 children aged 7-8 years across 24 classes in 11 primary schools in the Bordeaux school district in France.

Results show that the adaptive ZPDES curriculum outperformed the predefined linear curriculum on learning gains, and that adding choice to ZPDES further increased both intrinsic motivation and learning performance. In contrast, adding choice to the predefined linear curriculum reduced learning outcomes even though it improved subjective experience. The authors conclude that learner choice is beneficial when paired with an adaptive personalized system that keeps learners in an appropriate difficulty range, but can be distracting in a fixed linear curriculum.
quality_tier_rationale: This is a randomized controlled field study with a reasonably large sample and multiple conditions, which supports strong internal validity. However, it is a single study in one domain and the report provides limited detail on randomization/blinding and uses some marginal pairwise comparisons, so it falls short of blue-tier certainty.
impact_tier_rationale: The academic effect on math learning is statistically significant and of modest-to-meaningful magnitude (η²=0.034 for the key interaction, with clear pre/post gains and higher post-test scores under ZPDES). The study also reports meaningful motivational/emotional benefits, indicating a consequential intervention effect in a priority K-12 population.

interventions.use_case: adaptive math tutoring for 7-8 year-old children using a zone-of-proximal-development curriculum manager (ZPDES) with multi-armed bandit personalization, compared against a hand-designed linear curriculum; a second condition adds contextual learner choice of visual objects without changing task difficulty

finding.finding_summary: In a 4-arm RCT with 265 children (Predef n=62, PCO n=59, ZPDES n=76, ZCO n=68), the ITS improved math learning from pre- to post-test, and the adaptive ZPDES condition outperformed the predefined sequence. Reported marginal means show Predef improved from 6.83 to 8.36, whereas ZPDES improved from 6.74 to 9.38 on a 20-point math test; the algorithm × pre/post interaction was significant, F(1,261)=40.076, p=0.003, η²=0.034.
finding.measure: Pre/post math test score on 20-item money manipulation, decomposition, addition, and subtraction assessment
finding.std_deviation: Predef pre/post SD=0.353/0.396; ZPDES pre/post SD=0.344/0.363

finding.finding_summary: The choice feature improved students’ emotional experience and tended to improve motivation, especially when combined with ZPDES. Emotional valence was significantly higher with choice than without choice, F(1,261)=12.060, p=0.001, η²=0.044, and motivation showed a positive trend for choice, F(1,261)=3.449, p=0.064, η²=0.013, with the strongest motivation in ZCO (M=15.353) versus Predef (M=13.726).
finding.measure: Emotional Scale score and Vallerand motivation questionnaire
finding.std_deviation: Emotion SDs: choice=183.58, no choice=226.96; motivation SDs: ZCO=0.528, Predef=0.553
